one_liner: AOM's production AV1 encoder in C, built to be much faster than libaom at similar efficiency; no published speed numbers.
what_it_does: SVT-AV1 is an AV1 encoder library plus the SvtAv1EncApp command-line tool, aimed at everything from slow VOD encodes (presets M0-M3) to live and RTC encoding (presets M8 and up, --rtc). You call svt_av1_enc_init_handle, set_parameter, init, send_picture and get_packet. FFmpeg exposes it as -c:v libsvtav1 with -svtav1-params. It does not use libaom's aom_codec API and has no decoder: the decoder was removed in v2.1.1 (the last version with it is v2.1.0), so pair it with dav1d.
how_it_is_fast: The encoder runs as a pipeline of stateless 'processes' (picture analysis, motion estimation, rate control, mode decision, loop filters, entropy coding, packetization) that pass work through FIFO-based system resource managers. That gives parallelism at three levels: different stages at once, several pictures at once, and several segments of one picture at once. It does this without tiles, so in default CRF mode --lp 1 and --lp n produce the same output. Presets switch AV1 tools on or off along a documented curve; from M7 up, for example, it uses 64x64 superblocks, turns off filter intra, global motion (already off from M5), wedge and distance-weighted compound prediction (from M3), and the self-guided restoration filter (from M4). The hot kernels are hand-written SIMD: NASM and intrinsics from SSE2 to AVX2/AVX-512 on x86 (AVX-512 on by default since v2.3.0), and Neon, SVE and SVE2 on AArch64. The build scripts offer LTO and PGO.
when_to_use: You need AV1 output and libaom's encode time is the bottleneck: VOD or archival encodes at presets 4-6 on a many-core x86-64 server (the docs say about 16 cores are used fairly efficiently for 1080p at those presets).
Live, low-latency or RTC encoding with --rtc (CBR rate control, low-delay prediction structure, presets M7-M12 in RTC mode as of v3.1/v4.2).
FFmpeg-based transcoding pipelines through libsvtav1, including 10-bit and HDR (BT.2020/PQ/HLG metadata) and film-grain synthesis.
AVIF and still-image encoding with --avif (lower memory) and the still-image IQ tune added in v4.0.0.

Large-scale batch encoding where you can split the source into scene chunks and run several instances pinned to core sets (--pin, taskset, with a lower --lp per instance), as the parameter docs suggest.
when_not_to_use: You need measured evidence that it is faster than libaom, x265 or x264 on your workload: the repository publishes no numbers, only qualitative CHANGELOG lines, and its own comparison harness ships without results.
Decoding AV1: there is no decoder in current releases. Use dav1d.
Very high core counts on one 1080p stream: the docs say scaling drops off past about 16 cores at presets 4-6, and presets 0-3 parallelize worse. Chunk the video instead.

Sub-second-latency live encoding pinned to an old preset map: issue #2263 reports low-delay latency rising from 150-250 ms (v2.1.0, presets 11-12) to 4-5 s after the v3.0.0 preset remapping. Re-validate latency after every upgrade.

Projects whose license policy needs an OSI-approved license with a patent grant: the code is BSD-3-Clause-Clear (FSF-free but not OSI-approved, and it explicitly grants no patent rights), and patents come separately under the AOM Patent License 1.0, which has a defensive-termination clause.

integration.form: static or shared lib (CMake) plus the SvtAv1EncApp CLI; FFmpeg libsvtav1 wrapper
integration.dependencies: NASM 2.14+ (or yasm) for x86 builds; cpuinfo (system copy, or fetched and built in since v3.0.0); nothing else at runtime
integration.min_toolchain: C99, CMake 3.16+; GCC 5.4+ or Clang on Linux, Visual Studio 2017/2019 on Windows (per Build-Guide.md)
integration.platforms: x86-64 primary (SIMD from SSE2 up; AVX2 recommended, AVX-512 kernels built by default); AArch64 with Neon, SVE and SVE2 kernels; validated on Windows, Linux and macOS; any other target with a C99 compiler runs the C path
integration.thread_safety: Each encoder handle manages its own internal thread pools (--lp picks a parallelism level, not a thread count; issue #2317 notes many threads are created regardless). Running several encoder instances in one process has a history of hangs: v4.1 added mutexes for this (!2603, !2605, !2619), but issue #2186 (hang when only some instances use preset 8) and #2226 (crash under a fully loaded machine) are still open.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: it produces standard AV1 bitstreams that any AV1 decoder reads, but its API, presets and options differ from libaom's aomenc/aom_codec interface

gotchas: Preset numbers are not stable across releases: v1.7.0 shifted M2-M6 by one preset, v3.0.0 'repositioned the presets and removed one preset resulting in a max preset of M10', and v3.1.0 re-enabled M11/M12 for RTC. The CHANGELOG's 'M8 about x265 medium' (v0.8.7, 2021) and 'M12 about x264 veryfast' (v0.9, 2022) refer to old preset maps.
Public API breaks at major versions: v3.0.0 (issue 2217) and v4.0.0 removed fields, macros and deprecated structs. Pin the version and recheck callers on upgrade.
It never inserts keyframes at scene changes, whatever the scd setting (CommonQuestions.md); use an external scene splitter if you need them.

Open crash reports to check against your configuration: #2356 (SIGSEGV in svt_aom_blend_a64_mask_avx2 on v3.1.2 with GCC 13), #2395 (--hbd-mds 1 at preset 2 with 10-bit input) and #2396 (deblocking not signalled for non-reference frames when CDEF and restoration are off).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: It is the only C AV1 encoder catalogued for speed (rusty-av1-toolkit is a tuned rav1e), so pick it whenever the target format is AV1 and libaom is too slow; VVenC, Kvazaar and uavs3e serve VVC, HEVC and AVS3 instead. Pair it with the catalogued dav1d for decoding, since SVT-AV1 no longer ships a decoder.
verified_claims_summary: Nothing was measured on a reachable page. The CHANGELOG pairs SVT-AV1 presets with x265 medium (M8, v0.8.7) and x264 veryfast (M12, v0.9) at 'similar speed', with no clips, machine or method. The libaom comparison ('similar compression efficiency, significantly lower latency on multi-core', and the 10-50x figures in third-party guides) is known only from search snippets of blocked pages.
status_note: Very active (v4.2.0 released 2026-07-14, last activity 2026-10-03, 305 stars and 177 forks on GitLab, maintained by the AOM Software Implementation Working Group and used through FFmpeg), but the evidence is D-tier and the BSD-3-Clause-Clear license (not OSI-approved, patents via the separate AOM Patent License) is why the record is marked reference rather than copyable.
measurement_notes: There is an in-repo comparison harness that the verifier did not mention: test/benchmarking/ (Meta Platforms, 2025). run_comparison.sh, encode.py and configs/test_video_config.yaml build libaom (Release, plus a CONFIG_REALTIME_ONLY 'aomenc_rtc' build) and SVT-AV1 (build.sh --minimal-build --enable-lto) from source. The default config encodes a 360p set single-threaded in CBR low-delay mode: libaom at --cpu-used 7/9/11 as the BD-rate anchor (speed 11), SVT-AV1 at presets 9/10 and in RTC mode 9-12. Timing is user+sys CPU from /usr/bin/time -p, and PSNR/VMAF come from decoding with dav1d. No results are committed, so it gives no numbers for a retier. Before anyone uses its timings: the libaom command lines carry --psnr, so aomenc computes PSNR inside the timed run, while the standard svtav1 command does not. The harness README itself puts in-encoder PSNR at about 10-15% of SVT encode time, so this tilts any speed comparison toward SVT-AV1, by an amount not measured. Both libaom variants also run with --rt --usage=1 and a long list of disabled tools, so this is not a like-for-like default-mode comparison. Paper sources that could support a B retier are all on blocked hosts: SPIE 2020, 2021, 2022 and 2024, ICIP 2023 (arXiv 2307.05208, 'Encoder Complexity Control in SVT-AV1 by Speed-Adaptive Preset Switching'), arXiv 2401.16067 ('Encoding Time and Energy Model for SVT-AV1'), and the AOM SIWG common test conditions PDF. A Streaming Learning Center article 'SVT-AV1 vs. LibAOM' appears in search results but is a blocked blog (snippet only).
